Tatiana's teacher drew a $3 \times 3$ grid on the board, with zero in each cell. The students then took turns to pick a $2 \times 2$ square of four adjacent cells, and to add 1 to each of the numbers in the four cells. After a while, the grid looked like the diagram on the right (some of the numbers in the cells have been rubbed out.)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left is the initial 3×3 grid, and every cell is 0. On the right is the 3×3 grid after several operations, among which the visible numbers are: the middle of the top row is 18, the middle cell is 47, the left of the bottom row is 13, and the right of the bottom row is a question mark; some of the remaining cells are covered by gray or erased. Reasoning: In a 3×3 grid, there are four possible 2×2 blocks in total. Let the numbers of times they are selected be a, b, c, d respectively, corresponding respectively to the upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, and lower-right four 2×2 blocks. The middle cell of the top row will only be affected by the upper-left and upper-right two 2×2 blocks, so a+b=18. The left cell of the bottom row will only be affected by the lower-left 2×2 block, so c=13. The center cell will be affected by all four 2×2 blocks, so a+b+c+d=47. The required right cell of the bottom row will only be affected by the lower-right 2×2 block, therefore its value is d. Thus d=47-18-13=16.

method.method_draft: Read the right-hand final 3x3 grid from the image: top-middle is 18, center is 47, bottom-left is 13, and bottom-right is the question mark; other shown grey cells are rubbed out. From the text, each move adds 1 to one of the four possible 2x2 blocks in a 3x3 grid. Let the numbers of times these four 2x2 blocks were chosen be a, b, c, d for top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right respectively. Then top-middle equals a+b=18, bottom-left equals c=13, center equals a+b+c+d=47, and the desired bottom-right equals d. Subtract to get d=47-18-13=16.

method.method_draft: Read the image first: in the final grid the visible relevant numbers are 18 at the top-middle, 47 at the center, 13 at the bottom-left, and ? at the bottom-right. From the text, each operation is one of four 2x2 blocks. Observe an invariant contribution rule: after any single 2x2 move, the increase in the center cell is matched exactly by the increase in one of three cells: top-middle for a top-row 2x2 move, bottom-left for the bottom-left 2x2 move, or bottom-right for the bottom-right 2x2 move. Therefore throughout the process, center = top-middle + bottom-left + bottom-right. Substitute the visible values: 47 = 18 + 13 + ?, so ? = 16.

Reasoning: In a 3×3 grid, each move chooses one of the four possible 2×2 blocks. Every such move increases the center cell by 1. If the chosen 2×2 block is in the top row, then the top-middle cell also increases by 1. If it is the bottom-left 2×2 block, then the bottom-left cell increases by 1. If it is the bottom-right 2×2 block, then the bottom-right cell increases by 1. Thus, over the whole process, the center cell equals the sum of the top-middle, bottom-left, and bottom-right cells. So 47 = 18 + 13 + ?. Therefore ? = 47 - 18 - 13 = 16.
